text: A threat intelligence feed is a continuously updated stream of IOCs — malicious IPs, domains, file hashes — that someone else has already confirmed are bad. Today we'll look at where these feeds actually come from, how a SOC turns one into an automatic firewall block, and how feed context enriches an alert an analyst is already looking at.

A feed is just thousands of the IOCs we covered in Lesson 17, refreshed constantly, from sources that specialize in finding them faster than any single organization could on its own. The value isn't the list itself — it's that the list updates before an attacker's infrastructure ever reaches your network.

Feeds come from three common sources. Commercial vendors sell curated, high-confidence feeds built from their own research. ISACs are sector-specific groups — the financial sector's, the healthcare sector's — where member organizations pool what they're seeing. And open-source projects, run by the research community, publish IOCs for free. A mature SOC typically blends all three, because each tends to catch different things first.

A Threat Intelligence Platform, or TIP, is the tooling that ingests multiple feeds, deduplicates and scores them, and pushes the resulting blocklist to enforcement points automatically — most commonly the firewall. Report a malicious command-and-control IP, and within minutes any device on the network trying to reach it is blocked, before a human ever looks at it.

The second major use is enrichment. A bare SIEM alert saying a workstation connected to an external IP is far more useful once it carries feed context: that IP has been reported in forty other organizations' incidents this month as Cobalt Strike command-and-control. An analyst can skip research entirely and go straight to containment.

Feeds give a SOC automatic blocking and richer alerts, both built on the IOCs from Lesson 17. Next up, Lesson 19 covers STIX and TAXII — the real industry-standard pairing organizations actually use to share that threat intelligence with each other in the first place.
